title: Machine-learning design yields a high-strength printable aluminum alloy
summary: Hybrid CALPHAD/ICME calculations and Bayesian optimization selected an Al-Er-Zr-Y-Yb-Ni composition that was manufactured as powder and printed by laser powder bed fusion without the cracking reported for Al 7075. The preprint reports 50% greater strength after 400 °C aging than the strongest benchmark printable aluminum alloy. This is a measured material result, not component-scale qualification.
ai_technology: Hybrid CALPHAD/ICME; neural-network regression; Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Carnegie Mellon University

evidence.tested: The source reports the study-specific result summarized here.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and broader deployment or clinical benefit are not established by this source review.
evidence.ai_role: Simulation-derived features train a forward model and Bayesian optimization proposes compositions; the selected alloy is manufactured and mechanically tested.
